messages:
omar: Hey folks, quick newbie question. I merged two kubeconfigs (work and onboarding) by `KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config:~/Downloads/onboard-config kubectl config view --merge > ~/.kube/config` and now `kubectl config get-contexts` shows both contexts but `kubectl get ns` hits `Forbidden`. Any obvious misstep?

claire: Welcome Omar! Merging can be fine but double-check the current context: `kubectl config current-context`. If the context points to the onboarding cluster but your user is from the other kubeconfig, auth will fail. Run `kubectl config use-context <onboard-context>` or set `KUBECONFIG` explicitly.

omar: Current-context is `onboard-dev`. `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n infra` returns "no". How do I request view access for infra?

claire: We handle namespace access via the Access repo or portal. Easiest: open a tiny PR in infra/access-requests with a RoleBinding YAML (example in onboarding). Put your GH username, requested role `view`, namespaces, and reason. Tag @claire for quick review.

omar: Filed PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4950 — requested `view` in `infra` for debugging local deploys.

infra-bot: Access request PR #4950 created by omar. Automated checks passed. Reviewer requested: claire.

claire: Approved and applied. Gave `view` in `infra` for 14d. Try `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n infra` now.

taylor: FYI if you keep merged kubeconfigs, watch out for duplicated user names; I usually prefix the onboarding cluster entries before merging to avoid overwriting credentials.

omar: `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n infra` -> "yes". All good now, thanks everyone! :tada:`
